note: Narration templates for the guided tours. Figures come from {placeholders} filled from the live data; conclusions are chosen by rules in the app ({"by": fact, "cases": {...}}). The weekly tour agent may refine wording and choose examples, within the rules checked by tools/validate.py.

gap.title: Is AI shrinking the gap from research to change?

intro.say: Each arc is one research breakthrough, from a university, a government lab or industry. The arc starts when the research began and lands at the first product. A thinner arc then runs on to large-scale adoption.

yes: For example: {exTitle}. Research {exWhere} began in {exR}, the first product came in {exP}

cases.yes: , and it was in mainstream use by {exAdopt}.

cases.no: Select any arc to see its story.

say: Here is a century of change. Thinner arcs carry on to mainstream adoption

cases.shrunk: Overall, the typical gap has shrunk: {pre} years for research begun before 1970, {recent} for research since 2000.
cases.grown: Overall, the typical gap has grown: {pre} years for research begun before 1970, {recent} for research since 2000.
cases.flat: Overall, the typical gap has barely changed: {pre} years for research begun before 1970, {recent} for research since 2000.
cases.unclear: There is not yet enough data to say how the gap has changed overall.

say: But recent research has not all landed yet. Allowing for work still unfinished,

cases.holds: research since 2010 takes about {kmYears} years, still clearly quicker than research before 1970.
cases.weakens: research since 2010 takes about {kmYears} years, so it is not clearly quicker than research before 1970.
cases.tooEarly: it is too early to be sure.
cases.unclear: there is not yet enough data to tell.

gapchart.say: The gap-over-time chart follows this decade by decade, then adds scenarios beyond today, including AI and digital twins.

cases.ai: Since 2000, AI itself is the fastest field, at about {fastestYears} years.
cases.other: Since 2000, {fastestName} is fastest; AI ranks {aiRankWord} of {nFields}.

say: With one field selected, its sub-fields get their own tracks.

cases.faster: Since 2010, AI-driven work took {ai} years, against {oth} for the rest.
cases.slower: Since 2010, AI-driven work has taken longer: {ai} years, against {oth} for the rest.
cases.similar: Since 2010, AI-driven work took about as long as the rest: {ai} years against {oth}.
cases.unclear: There are not yet enough AI-driven milestones to compare.

cases.faster: Ahead, AI-assisted work is expected to take {aiOut} years, against {convOut} for conventional work.
cases.slower: Ahead, the estimates do not show AI landing sooner.
cases.similar: Ahead, the estimates show little difference.

say: So, is AI shrinking the gap?

cases.0: Not yet: none of the four measures here points to yes.
cases.1: Not really: only one of the four measures here points to yes.
cases.2: Partly: two of the four measures here, half, point to yes.
cases.3: Probably: three of the four measures here point to yes.
cases.4: Yes: all four measures here point to yes.

say: The answer updates as new evidence arrives.

horizon.title: What AI-assisted products are on the horizon for the energy system?

intro.say: The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) has set out a vision for a clean energy system supported by AI, grouped into five areas. Diamonds mark the related arcs, which play here from 1980.

radar.say: The Vision radar shows how ready each area's technologies are: {nResearch} in research, {nPilot} piloting, {nCommercial} in first commercial use and {nScale} at scale. {nGB} are deployed in Great Britain.

cases.some: New in the last three months, found by the agents: {newCount}, including {newTitle}. Mark them as reviewed, and next time you will see only what has arrived since.
cases.none: Nothing new has arrived in the last three months. Mark the radar as reviewed, and next time you will see only what has arrived since.

cases.some: Expected within five years: {nextCount}, the soonest being {nextTitle}, around {nextYear}. {busiestArea} has the most in the pipeline.
cases.none: In the current data, no products are expected to arrive within five years.

changes.say: Data changes lists everything the agents add or correct each week. Here it shows only changes linked to the vision.

slide.say: For a briefing, the PowerPoint report window creates a one-slide summary of all five areas, ready to drop into a deck.

say: So, what is on the horizon?

cases.busy: A busy pipeline, and the radar shows which areas are closest to everyday use.
cases.steady: A steady pipeline, with the radar showing which areas are moving.
cases.quiet: Not much yet in the data, so watch the radar as the agents search each week.

intro.say: New technology opens new ways for attackers to get in. Of the technologies here, {attackPct} percent widen the attack surface, from smart devices at the edge of the grid to AI agents.

say: The Cyber lens shows how long security took to catch up:

cases.slow: typically {lag} years after a technology arrived, a long time to leave systems exposed.
cases.moderate: typically {lag} years after a technology arrived.
cases.fast: typically within {lag} years of a technology arriving.
cases.unclear: the data does not yet show this clearly.

cases.some: Since 2010, some technologies have arrived with no security response yet in their category. There are {gapCount} so far, including {gapTitle}.
cases.none: In this data, every technology since 2010 has seen a security response in its category.

example.say: Each card names the risk and suggests ways to reduce it, linked to the NCSC's Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), Ofgem's CAF Overlay, NIST, NERC CIP and IEC 62443.

cases.some: A guidance agent records new security guidance every week, CAF and Ofgem first. The latest: {guideTitle}.
cases.none: A guidance agent records new security guidance every week, CAF and Ofgem first.

caution.say: This is AI research to prompt discussion, not security advice. Always engage qualified experts, and your regulator where relevant.

cases.improving: It is catching up faster than it used to.
cases.worsening: It is taking longer to catch up than it used to.

intro.say: Research does not just change products; it can also make fortunes. Time to a fortune follows founders from starting a company to the listing, sale or valuation that made them rich.

research.say: Of {nFortunes} fortunes here, {nResearch} began in a university or research lab. Gold rings mark those research founders.

cases.faster: The road is getting shorter: about {preYears} years for companies founded before 1970, against {recentYears} for those founded since 2015.
cases.slower: The road is getting longer: about {preYears} years for companies founded before 1970, against {recentYears} for those founded since 2015.
cases.similar: The road is about as long as ever: about {preYears} years for companies founded before 1970, against {recentYears} for those founded since 2015.
cases.unclear: There are not yet enough fortunes from recently founded companies to compare eras.

fastest.say: Sorted by speed, the fastest so far is {fastestCo}, in {fastestTime}.

cases.faster: Filter by country: research that began in the UK reached a product in {ukYears} years, faster than the {rowYears} elsewhere.
cases.slower: Filter by country: research that began in the UK took {ukYears} years to reach a product, against {rowYears} elsewhere.
cases.similar: Filter by country: UK research reached a product in about the same time as elsewhere, {ukYears} years against {rowYears}.
cases.unclear: Filter by country to compare UK research with the rest of the world.

uni.say: Gold rings also mark university projects still under way: {nUni} of them. They could be the next generation of breakthroughs, and perhaps of fortunes.

table.say: The Table lists every milestone. Sort by any column, such as the gap, and select a row for its story.

cases.similar: the journey takes about as long as ever.
cases.unclear: it is too early to say whether the journey is getting faster or slower.

intro.say: This model is maintained by AI agents that run every week. It holds {nMilestones} milestones so far.

research.say: A research agent searches every field, and each vision area of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), for new breakthroughs and products. The Data changes view lists everything it adds.

qa.say: A second agent checks every find independently. It needs more than one source, and the quoted evidence must really appear on the page. Nothing is ever deleted.

more.say: Further agents track new security guidance and refresh these walk-throughs. Every change must pass automatic checks before it is published.

say: Data quality shows that {pctSourceCited} percent of records now cite a checked source.

cases.scored: Forecasts are scored once their outcome is known: {fcResolved} so far.
cases.none: Each forecast is recorded and will be scored once its outcome is known.

labels.say: Every record says how it was checked: source-cited, AI-compiled or an AI estimate. You can filter by these.

arrange.say: Arrangements set the windows up for exploring, presenting, analysis or a DESNZ briefing. You can save any view, or share it as a link.

answer.say: Help and the i buttons explain each feature. Because AI maintains this model, it may contain errors, so check anything important against the original sources.
